explanation: Advance the leading pointer k nodes from the head while a trailing pointer starts at a dummy predecessor. Move both until the leading pointer is null; the trailing pointer then precedes the kth-last node.
timeComplexity: O(n) Both pointers move forward at most n links.
spaceComplexity: O(1) Only a dummy predecessor and two pointers are needed.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/DeleteKthLastFromList.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: The leading pointer stays k+1 links ahead of the trailing pointer including the dummy offset. When it becomes null, exactly k nodes follow the trailing pointer, so its successor is the kth-last. Bypassing that successor removes precisely the target, including when it is the head.
walkthrough: For [7,5,9,2] and k=4, the kth-last node is the head 7. The dummy predecessor bypasses it, returning [5,9,2].
edgeCases: k equal to list length removes the head.
The contract supplies a valid positive k.
